issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case identifiers (e.g., 'lecture_name', 'number_of_inscribed_students') but the constructor and all methods refer to camelCase fields (e.g., 'lectureName', 'numberOfInscribedStudents'). This naming mismatch causes unresolved symbol errors and prevents the class from compiling, and it contradicts the attribute names shown in the problem statement UML and text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute identifiers consistent across the class. Rename the declared fields to the camelCase names used throughout the constructor and methods (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or alternatively update all usages to match the declared snake_case names. Ensure the field names match the UML and problem statement so the class compiles and students can follow the intended design.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution's Lecture.java declares private fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while its constructor and methods use the camelCase identifiers. This mismatch between declared field names and the identifiers used throughout the class causes a semantic and practical naming inconsistency that will confuse students and results in a non-compilable/ambiguous implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent camelCase attribute names across all artifacts to match the UML and problem statement. Rename the private fields in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; and ensure all constructor parameters and methods reference these same identifiers (or alternatively make all references use the declared snake_case names, but prefer camelCase to match the UML and Java conventions). Also ensure the template's Lecture.java guidance and any examples use the same names.
